newsitem.title: USA: U.S. EPA calls oil industry warning "odd at best".
newsitem.headline: U.S. EPA calls oil industry warning "odd at best".

text.p: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency said Tuesday the oil industry's idea that the government was out to get it by creating new agencies unaccountable to no one was unfounded.
"This theory is odd at best," said an EPA official, commenting on a speech by Charles DiBona, president of the American Petroleum Institute.

DiBona Monday accused the government of directing a "stealth" attack against the oil industry using new multi-state and international groups to recommend ways to protect the environment without weighing the economic costs.
"As a result, destructive policies can sneak through the nation's political defense, wreaking economic havoc before we know what hit us," he said at the API's annual meeting.
But the EPA said bodies such as the 37-state Ozone Transport Assessment Group were simply advisory.

"In no case, however, do outside recommendations bind our policy decisions, which are always based on providing the best protection of public health and the environment through the most cost-effective means possible," the EPA official said.
"In all cases, the EPA wants to hear the public's opinions, including those of the oil industry," he said.
